text: Beneath the looks of rich and show-off kids, lies the hard truth of a regiment that has never lost a fight. \\nWarcry: "Liberty! Equity! Liquidity!"
Rod-rigo, Rod-rigo\\n marching through the land\\n Rod-rigo, Rod-rigo\\n with his honest band\\n Feared by the greedy\\n Loved by the needy\\n Rod-rigo, Rod-rigo, Rod-rigo!
From desperation, hardships and tolling training grew that regiment capable of besting Sauri and Vampires alike by pike, sword and crossbow. "Trained in Lustria", in fact.
Exiled guardians of a sacred shrine, the Leopards always send back everything they earned. Taking out necessary expenses such as fine wine, silk shirts and pasta sauce.
They're barely even proper soldiers. No discipline, no uniforms and the worst breath you've ever smelt on anyone that wasn't an Ogre. So why do they fight like the personal guard of the Emperor?
The swish of a cloak here, a twirl there, a dagger in the ribs of the bedazzled opponent. Determined, efficient, fashionable, like Vespero and his duellists.
Each trooper in Maximilian Damark's company must get a bull's eye on a coin at 300 paces to demonstrate their skill. It doesn't take a genius to guess what they can do in battle.
An unbeaten regiment forged by Borgio's exploits, the mere sight of the Besiegers in their heavy plate is enough to make surrender an option. \\n"Invincibility at no extra charge."
The warrior sisterhood of Lustria hasn't really grasped the fine concept of mercenary service. To them, their hirer is just as weak as the target they have crushed...
After the loss of the monastery of Saint Origo in the heathen lands, the "Frothers" crusade with sweet abandon under blood-red banners. \\n"Only the Sword Purifies."
Out of fate, prophecies and curses ride the Desert Dogs into everybody else's nightmares of blood and sand.

In a parody of his former mercenary career, Richter Kreugar is cursed to live as an undead, to be slain in battle only to rise again in the morning. So he marches on, with his silent regiment of undead companions...
Even amongst fellow Dark Elves, Mengil and his merry band would be considered excessively sanguinary. Truly, one must be properly desperate to hire such a company of heavily armed cannibals.
A self-exiled Prince of Caledor, Asarnil glides above foreign battlefields from atop the great green dragon Deathfang and his own offended pride.
Tasked with the retrieval of lost plaques in the Old World, these Great Crested skinks ride rare and dangerous Horned Ones and are guided by their leader's visions.
Bronzino's crews are experts at maneuvering light artillery on the battlefield for devastating effect. \\n\\n The biggest bang for your bucks!
These "Magnificent men in their flying machines" are daring daredevils and marksmen who fly on canvas wings and snatch victory from above.
